name: EmotionPrompt (Psychology-Inspired Emotional Stimulus)
executive_summary: Append a short, psychology-derived emotional-stimulus sentence to an unchanged zero-shot prompt — a near-zero-cost addition shown to outperform plain zero-shot and Zero-Shot-CoT baselines across tasks and models.
description: Grounded in established psychology theory (social identity theory, social cognition theory) rather than ad hoc phrasing, EmotionPrompt appends one of a small set of tested emotional-stimulus sentences to a prompt, using the same underlying task template otherwise unchanged. Evaluated against plain zero-shot and Zero-Shot-CoT baselines across 8 tasks and multiple models (ChatGPT, Vicuna-13b, Bloom, T5), with reported improvements in truthfulness and informativeness as well as raw performance, and a human study reporting a 10.9% average improvement across performance, truthfulness, and responsibility metrics. Notable as one of the cheapest interventions in this catalog — a single appended sentence, no additional calls, no exemplars, no fine-tuning.
when_to_use: As a near-free addition to an existing zero-shot or Zero-Shot-CoT prompt when squeezing out additional performance is worth testing, given the marginal cost is close to zero.
Generative tasks where truthfulness/informativeness, not just raw accuracy, matters.
when_not_to_use: Tasks where prompt tone must remain strictly neutral/formal for domain reasons (e.g. some regulated or clinical contexts) — the emotional framing may be inappropriate regardless of any performance gain.

As a substitute for more substantive reasoning-elicitation techniques when the task genuinely needs multi-step decomposition — this is a low-cost add-on, not a replacement for chain-of-thought or self-consistency.
known_pitfalls: Effect size and which specific stimulus sentence works best is somewhat model- and task-dependent; the paper tests a fixed small set of stimuli rather than claiming any emotional framing helps.

primary_source.authors: Li, Wang, Zhang, Zhu, Hou, Lian, Luo, Yang, Xie
primary_source.title: Large Language Models Understand and Can be Enhanced by Emotional Stimuli

variables.name: base_zero_shot_prompt
variables.description: The unmodified underlying zero-shot (or Zero-Shot-CoT) prompt

variables.name: emotional_stimulus_sentence
variables.description: A tested psychology-derived stimulus sentence appended after the task prompt
variables.example: This is very important to my career. You'd better be sure.

usage_templates.reproducibility_note: A single LLM call (or a fixed sequence of them) with no external system dependency; running this template again at temperature 0 against the same model version should reproduce the same output.
